title: UFO Moviez's in-cinema ad revenue grows 3% in Q2, total advertising income remains flat
description: New Delhi: UFO Moviez India's in-cinema advertising revenue grew 3% year-on-year to Rs 33.4 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 32.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. However, total advertising revenue, including Caravan Talkies, remained almost unchanged at Rs 33.4 crore, against Rs 33.5 crore a year earlier. The September quarter saw a slowdown in advertising growth compared with the first quarter, when UFO's in-cinema advertising revenue had increased by approximately 34%. Corporate and hyperlocal advertising revenue rose 3% to Rs 27.2 crore in Q2 FY27, while government and public sector advertising revenue increased 4% to Rs 6.2 crore. According to the company's investor presentation, average advertising revenue per screen stood at Rs 85,142 during the quarter, compared with Rs 85,526 a year earlier. The average number of advertising minutes sold per show per screen remained unchanged at 4.55 minutes. Advertising contributed 26% of UFO's revenue from operations during the quarter, compared with 30% in Q2 FY26. Overall revenue grows 17%, profit declines 15% UFO reported a 17% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 129.9 crore in Q2 FY27, primarily supported by higher revenue from its exhibitor business. Revenue from operations increased to Rs 129.4 crore from Rs 110.8 crore a year earlier. Revenue from exhibitors grew 44% to Rs 62 crore, compared with Rs 43 crore in Q2 FY26. Within this segment, product sales rose 66% to Rs 42.2 crore from Rs 25.4 crore. Lease rental income declined 3% to Rs 14.7 crore, while other operating revenue from exhibitors increased to Rs 5.2 crore from Rs 2.6 crore. Revenue from distributors remained largely unchanged at Rs 34 crore, compared with Rs 34.3 crore in the year-ago quarter. Content delivery charges declined 3% to Rs 23.9 crore, while virtual print fee service revenue increased 11% to Rs 5.7 crore. Despite the increase in revenue, consolidated net profit declined 15% to Rs 6.4 crore from Rs 7.5 crore a year earlier. EBITDA fell 2% to Rs 21.3 crore, while profit before tax declined 10% to Rs 9.6 crore. Rajesh Mishra, Executive Director and Group CEO, UFO Moviez, said theatrical performance during the quarter was influenced by a mix of major releases, sleeper hits and films that struggled to attract audiences. "Q2 FY27 highlighted the importance of content with theatrical audiences: a combination of major releases drew strong footfalls and sleeper hits that exceeded expectations, alongside films that struggled to connect with viewers. This reinforces the importance of content diversity and audience word-of-mouth in shaping box office performance," Mishra said. He added that the company's partnership with DCDC would open opportunities to expand the delivery of Indian content across North America. First-half cinema advertising revenue rises 17% UFO's advertising performance was stronger over the first six months of FY27. In-cinema advertising revenue increased 17% year-on-year to Rs 70 crore in H1 FY27, compared with Rs 59.7 crore in the corresponding period last year. Corporate and hyperlocal advertising revenue grew 15% to Rs 55.7 crore, while government and PSU advertising increased 29% to Rs 14.3 crore. Total advertising revenue, including Caravan Talkies, rose 15% to Rs 70.7 crore from Rs 61.5 crore. Average advertising revenue per screen for the half-year increased to Rs 1,75,146 from Rs 1,56,761. The average number of advertising minutes sold per show per screen declined to 4.29 from 4.41. The share of advertising revenue paid to exhibitors declined to 56.48% in H1 FY27, compared with 60.70% in H1 FY26. For the first half, consolidated revenue grew 10% to Rs 241.7 crore, while EBITDA declined 2% to Rs 40.2 crore. Net profit fell 14% to Rs 12.1 crore from Rs 14.1 crore. Advertising network stands at 3,946 screens As of September 30, 2026, UFO had advertising rights across 3,946 cinema screens, comprising 2,606 multiplex screens and 1,340 single screens across 1,330 cities and towns. The network stood at 4,049 screens at the end of FY26. During the first half of FY27, multiplex screens increased from 2,597 to 2,606, while single screens declined from 1,452 to 1,340. The company's advertising network has gradually shifted towards multiplexes. These accounted for 66% of its total advertising screens at the end of September 2026, compared with 64% at the end of FY26. UFO's investor presentation also showed that the share of quarterly advertising revenue paid to exhibitors declined to 54.07% from 54.95% a year earlier.
